correctness.rationale: At \((0,0)\) the joint event is exactly \(q^{\xi}\ge0\), hence has probability \(1/2\). For every \(z>0\), the event is exactly the interval \(-z\le q^{\xi}\le\rho/z-z\), giving probability \(\Phi(\rho/z-z)-\Phi(-z)\). Strict monotonicity of \(\Phi\) yields the stated minimum \(g(z)\). As \(z\downarrow0\), the inverse-CDF argument tends to \(1\), so \(g(z)/z\to+\infty\). A convex feasible set containing the origin and \((z_0,g(z_0))\) would contain every scaled point \((tz_0,tg(z_0))\), contradicting the minimal-boundary inequality for sufficiently small \(t>0\). All divisions are restricted to \(z>0\), and the origin is treated separately.

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly identifies convexity of the joint feasible set as a challenging open question. The counterexample resolves the universal-convexity question negatively in the smallest dimension, under the same regular Gaussian and positive-definite-matrix setting where the separate model has a convex reformulation. The exact boundary formula also identifies the structural source of failure: an infinite radial slope at the feasible median-probability origin. The restriction to \(p=1/2\) is scientifically material and is stated rather than hidden.
